name: Void
label: Dischord
lede: Four kids from a planned suburb in Maryland, each playing as fast as he could and not always at the same time, and one side of a split LP that people are still trying to explain.

eras.title: Nothing to do in a model town
eras.text: Columbia, Maryland was one of the first planned communities in the country: tidy lawns, organized everything, thirty miles north of Washington. Dischord's own history calls it the perfect birthplace for a band as completely chaotic as Void.

q: Your lawn had to look a certain way.
years.h: A band named for a Black Sabbath song
years.p: Four Columbia High School kids start Void, taking the name from Black Sabbath's Into the Void.
years.xp: There wasn't much to do in Columbia besides sports and hanging around, as Dupree tells it, so any excuse to get to a show in D.C. or Baltimore was a good one. Stover's road into the scene ran through Oddfellows Hall in Towson, where he saw [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]] and met [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]].

years.cap: Void at the Wilson Center, where they made their debut.
years.p: Void debut at the Wilson Center, and D.C. takes in the suburban band right away. Each member is playing his own part as fast as humanly possible, not necessarily together. Some hear noise. Others hear something nobody else is doing.

eras.title: Two sessions in two months
eras.text: Void were barely out of their first year of shows when they cut thirty songs across two sessions. One vanished for three decades. The other put them on Dischord's first compilation.

years.h: Twenty songs at Hit and Run
years.p: Steve Carr records a 20-song session at Hit and Run Studios. It stays in a box until 2011, and Dupree later admits he doesn't remember recording most of it.

A month later the band goes to Inner Ear in Arlington and cuts ten songs, eight of them repeats from November. This session gives up the Flex Your Head tracks and, a decade later, the Condensed Flesh seven-inch.

eras.title: Half an LP with Faith
eras.text: 1982 was Void's year on record. They made the Dischord sampler, played New York, and split an LP with Faith: two bands, two approaches to speed, one sleeve.

years.p: Dehumanized, Authority and My Rules go on Dischord's compilation, next to [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]], [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]] and [[SOA|e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb]].

years.h: Back to Inner Ear, this time with Don Zientara
years.p: Don Zientara records Void's half of the split at Inner Ear. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] had pitched pairing them with [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]], and the band was happy to be part of the Dischord family.

years.cap: Void on the road in the Northeast, 1982.
years.h: Out of Maryland and into CBGB
years.p: Void start touring the Northeast, and the Bowery room is one of the stops. The band that couldn't find anything to do at home is now taking its racket to New York.
Twelve Void songs on one side, [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]] on the other. Critic Doug Mosurock later called Void's side quintessential American hardcore.
years.xp:
The two halves play like an argument. Faith are tight and furious. Void sound like four people falling down a staircase in formation, which is exactly what their fans came for.

The record kept a long life after both bands were gone: Dischord reissued it in 1985 and again in a remastered edition in 2008.

eras.title: The album nobody put out
eras.text: Void signed with Touch and Go and made a full album. Then the band ended, and the record stayed on the shelf, where the bootleggers found it and a few future heavy bands learned from it.

years.h: A deal with Touch and Go, and an album that stays in the can
years.p: Void sign with Touch and Go and record an album's worth of songs. By the time it could come out the band is gone, and label owner Corey Rusk isn't interested in releasing an album by a band that no longer exists.
years.xp:
By the time the record could have come out, Void were over, and Rusk had no reason to put out an album nobody would tour. Tapes got around anyway, and bootleggers circulated the session as Potions for Bad Dreams. According to Wikipedia, citing Stover's interview with Vice, [[White Zombie|cfe572bf-840f-4bed-934a-f69f4b1e90d4]] and [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] have said it shaped their own sound.

Asked about it decades later, Stover said some things are better left unreleased. Dupree was blunter.

years.p: A July 1983 show is recorded. Two songs from it will close out Sessions 1981-83 nearly thirty years later.
Dischord dates the end to fall 1984. Of the four, only Dupree keeps making music.

eras.title: The legend grows without them
eras.text: With the band gone, the records did the work. Dischord brought the split back, and a small label finally gave the Inner Ear session its own seven-inch.

years.p: Songs from the December 1981 Inner Ear session finally get their own seven-inch, including Black, Jewish & Poor and War Hero.

eras.title: Emptying the vaults
eras.text: Void's afterlife picked up speed in the 2000s: the loss of their drummer, a remaster, and a Dischord archive release built around twenty songs nobody outside the band had heard.

years.p: Void's drummer dies of an apparent heart attack, Dischord reported. He had been working on the set of HBO's The Wire.
years.xp: Finnegan kept the beat under Void's controlled collapse on every record the band made. His family held the viewing in Ellicott City, Maryland, not far from Columbia, and asked for donations to the Fisher House at Walter Reed in place of flowers.

years.p: Dischord puts out a digitally remastered edition of the split.
The lost Hit and Run session, the Inner Ear tapes, two Faith/Void outtakes and two live songs from 1983, mixed by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and pressed on blue vinyl.

[[Bubba Dupree|faa35f26-bda4-4dd0-9d92-121e616d955a]], who spent the 1990s and 2000s guesting with Soundgarden, Moby and [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]], joins 3rd Secret, the Seattle band built around former members of Nirvana and Soundgarden.
Eye 95 presses a 30th anniversary edition on translucent gold-orange vinyl.
